In Re.: IA No.:CAN/2/2024 This is an application for expunge the name of respondent No. 4.
Learned advocate appearing on behalf of the respondents submits that the respondent No.4 expired on 27.12.2022 during the pendency of the instant appeal.
So, he prayed for necessary order so that the name of the respondent No. 4 may be expunged from the Cause Title of the Memo of the Appeal.
Mr. Bhattacharyya further submits that the legal heirs of the respondent No. 4 are already on the record.
Considering the submission, the application being CAN 2 of 2024 is disposed of.
Department is directed to expunge the name of respondent No. 4 from the Cause Title of the Memo of the Appeal within a fortnight.

Additional District Judge, Fast Track, 2nd Court, Tamluk, Purba Medinipur, in MAC Case No. 29 of 2021.

sentences.text: The brief facts of the case is that the victim of this case, namely, one Biswanath Jana on 04.12.2020 at about 5.00 P.M. along with his daughter was standing at Deulbarh on NH-6 at the left side of the road for proceeding towards Bardabarh at that time one vehicle bearing No. WB- 30AE/4818 (Maruti Suzuki) which was going in a rash and negligent manner towards Kolaghat side dashed the victim with great force.
Due to the effect of such accident the victim sustained severe grievous injury all over his body specially on his head.
Thereafter, the victim was shifted to a near Nursing Home and he succumbed to his injuries on 19th December, 2020.
The widow, minor daughter and mother of the deceased preferred an application before the learned tribunal under Section 166 of M.V. Act for getting compensation.
The claim case was contested by the Insurance Company by filing written statement.

After hearing the parties and after receiving the evidences the learned tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs. 51,19,288/- in favour of the claimants towards the compensation and directed the Insurance Company to pay the compensation.
Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said award the instant appeal has been preferred by the Insurance Company.

Ms. Paul learned advocate appearing on behalf of the Insurance Company submits that the Insurance Company has challenged the award only on the ground that the so-called offending vehicle was not at all involved in the alleged accident.
He submits that the alleged accident was happened on 4th December, 2020 but the FIR was lodged only on 20th December, 2020.
Ms. Paul further submits that the FIR disclosed that the accident was happened by one unknown vehicle.
The police paper not clearly disclosed how the present vehicle was involved in the alleged accident.
She further submits that there are discrepancies in the evidences of claimants.

Moreover,
the charge-sheet also not clearly disclosed the antecedent of the present offending vehicle with the alleged accident.
She submits that the seizure list as well as the other police papers is not beyond doubt for the involvement of the present vehicle in the alleged accident.

Learned advocate appearing on behalf of the claimants Mr. Bhattacharyya submits that the ground to challenge the award only on the basis of non-involvement of the offending vehicle was raised before the learned tribunal.
The learned tribunal has specifically passed an observation that the offending vehicle was very well involved in the alleged accident.
The Insurance Company did not produce the single witness to contradict the evidentiary values of PWs.
He further submits that the investigation of police as well as the final report specifically disclosed the involvement of the present offending vehicle in the alleged accident.
So, he submits that the instant appeal is not maintainable.
Heard the learned advocate perused the evidences on records as well as the ground of appeal.

It is the case of the claimants that the accident was happened on 04.12.2020 at about 5.00 P.M. over NH-6 when the offending vehicle bearing No. WB-30AE/4818 dashed the victim PW-1 i.e. one of the daughter of the victim stated that she was present with her father at the time of accident when the National Insurance Co. sentences.text: However, during the further cross examination on recall the PW-1 again said that she did not see the accident in her own eyes.
PW-2 is one of the eye witness who disclosed that the offending vehicle bearing No. WB-30AE/4818 dashed the victim.
During the cross examination, the evidentiary value of PW-2 was not shaken by the Insurance Company.

One document was exhibited on behalf of the Insurance Company (exhibit-A) wherein the PW-1 has stated before the investigator of the Insurance Company that she did not witness the accident but after the accident he reached at the spot.
The FIR was lodged by the PW-1 disclosing the fact that she along with her father was standing along NH-6 when the accident happened.
The investigation of the police disclosed that during the course of investigation, the police reached at the P.O. and examined the available witnesses.
It appears that the C.S. witness No. 2 is the eye witness (P.W.-2) of this case who disclosed the identity of the vehicle.
It further appears from the seizure list that on 3rd January, 2020 the vehicle was seized on production by the owner of the offending vehicle.

Considering the entire scenario of the facts it appears that the accident happened on 04.12.2020, the victim died on 09.12.2020, on the next day i.e. on 20.12.2020 the FIR was lodged regarding involvement of an unknown vehicle, thereafter on 3rd January, 2021 the offending vehicle was seized on production by the owner.
It further appears that the driver surrendered before the learned CJM concerned admitting his guilt.
Considering the entire scenario it appears to me that there may have some discrepancies in the evidence of PW-1 but the involvement of the offending vehicle is not at all disputed.
It further appears to me that the C.S. witness No. 2 is cited as eye witness of this case who stated the involvement of the offending vehicle of the alleged accident.
The evidence of eye witness could not contradicted by the Insurance Company by producing cogent or believable evidence.
Thus, I find no justification to entertain the instant appeal.
Considering the all aspects, the appeal appears to be not meritorious.

The Insurance Company is directed to pay the compensation as awarded by the tribunal together with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of filing of the claim application through the office of the learned Registrar General, High Court Calcutta within six weeks from the date of passing of this order.
On such deposit the office of the learned Registrar General, High Court, Calcutta is directed to disburse the same in the name of the claimant respondent Nos.1, 2 and 3 equally as early as possible.
The payment of compensation is subject to ascertainment of payment of deficit Court Fees.
The office of the learned tribunal shall act upon the certified copy of this order to receive the deficit court fees, if any.
The applications being FMA 444 of 2024 is disposed of.
